## This tag leaks credentials. Do not use it.

It fixes eight defects found in the first audit round, including both of 0.1.0's
criticals, and then introduces two of its own.

**It stays resolvable on purpose.** Deleting a tag buys nothing against an attacker, since
clones, forks and cached commit views all survive it, and it breaks anyone already pinned
here. The disclosure record is the reason to trust the current release, so it is not being
quietly dropped.

**Be precise about whose credentials leaked.** The library failed to redact ITS USERS'
secrets: a credential a caller passed into `SecretRedactor.redact` could survive the
redactor and reach the model. No credential belonging to the author has ever been in this
repository, and every credential-shaped string under `Tests/` is synthetic.

## What it fixed

- **PEM blocks are consumed whole**, header through footer, rather than the header alone.
- **The injection fence carries a random id** in both tags, so a forged
  `</untrusted_data>` closer written by the untrusted text itself no longer matches.
- Six further defects from the same round.

## What is still wrong with it

- **The AWS secret access key leaks in full.** Dropping `/` from the entropy alphabet to
  protect file paths also dropped it from standard base64, which is `A-Za-z0-9+/`. That
  blinded the generic pass to the half of the AWS credential pair that actually grants
  access. Fixed in 0.3.0, which carries leaks of its own.
- **Redaction is quadratic on attacker-chosen input.** The PEM pattern's lazy scan means
  every `BEGIN` marker rescans the rest of the document. 1.2 MB of hostile input took 72
  seconds. Fixed in 0.2.1.

## What to use instead

**0.6.1**, or at minimum 0.5.0, which is the first tag with no known credential leak. Note
that the module is `GruxKit` up to and including 0.5.0 and `Grux` from 0.6.0 onward.

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/dotcomjack/grux.git", from: "0.6.1")
.product(name: "Grux", package: "grux")
```

## Full record

The complete narrative, including the wrong first attempts, is in
[CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/dotcomjack/grux/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). The README
section [Earlier tags leak credentials](https://github.com/dotcomjack/grux#earlier-tags-leak-credentials)
lists what each of the six leaking tags does.
